views.name: film_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  title,
  description,
  release_year,
  language_id,
  original_language_id,
  rental_duration,
  CAST(rental_rate AS REAL) AS rental_rate,
  CAST(length AS INTEGER) AS length,
  CAST(replacement_cost AS REAL) AS replacement_cost,
  rating,
  special_features,
  last_update
FROM film
views.description: Normalized film-level projection with key descriptive attributes and canonical numeric casts for common measures. Useful as a clean film dimension for joins, aggregation, and filtering. | Use for: Compare average rental_rate, length, or replacement_cost by category/language/rating; Filter films by release_year, rating, or feature and join to inventory/rental; Build film lists for recommendations or content catalogs

views.name: actor_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  actor_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  last_update
FROM actor
views.description: One-row-per-actor projection preserving actor identifiers and name attributes. Use when joining actor info to film_actor or reporting on actors. | Use for: List actors in a film or category; Count films per actor or rank actors by film appearances; Join actor names into cast lists

views.name: film_actor_bridge
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  actor_id,
  film_id,
  last_update
FROM film_actor
views.description: Bridge table mapping films to actors (one row per film-actor). Preserve keys for safe joins and include last_update for freshness checks. | Use for: Find all actors for a film or all films for an actor; Aggregate number of actors per film or films per actor; Build cast lists when joined to actor_name and film_basic

views.name: film_category_bridge
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  category_id,
  last_update
FROM film_category
views.description: Bridge table mapping films to categories (one row per film-category). Preserve keys for joining to category and film tables. | Use for: Count films per category or categories per film; Join categories to film_basic for category-level analysis; Filter films by category for downstream join to inventory/rental

views.name: inventory_by_film_store
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  store_id,
  COUNT(inventory_id) AS total_copies,
  MAX(last_update) AS last_update
FROM inventory
GROUP BY
  film_id,
  store_id
views.description: Aggregate inventory counts per film per store (one row per film+store) with total_copies. Useful for stock, availability, and store-level supply analyses. | Use for: Which films have the most copies at each store?; Join inventory availability to rental history by film and store; Compute stock coverage and identify understocked films per store

views.name: rental_facts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rental_id,
  rental_date,
  inventory_id,
  customer_id,
  return_date,
  staff_id,
  last_update
FROM rental
views.description: Denormalized rental-level fact rows with core foreign keys and timing/return info. Use as the base fact table for revenue and usage analyses when joined to payment, customer, inventory, and film. | Use for: Analyze rental counts/timelines per customer/film/store; Compute rental durations and late returns when joined with inventory and film; Join to payment to compute revenue per rental

views.name: payment_by_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_count,
  SUM(CAST(amount AS REAL)) AS total_amount,
  MAX(payment_date) AS last_payment_date
FROM payment
GROUP BY
  customer_id
views.description: Aggregate payments per customer with total_amount and payment_count. Useful for customer lifetime value, segmentation, and join to customer dimension. | Use for: Compute customer lifetime value and top-paying customers; Segment customers by recency, frequency, monetary (RFM); Join payment aggregates to customer demographics

views.name: customer_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  store_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  email,
  address_id,
  active,
  create_date,
  last_update
FROM customer
views.description: One-row-per-customer projection preserving identity, contact, store affiliation, active flag and creation timestamp. Useful when joining customers to payments, rentals, and addresses. | Use for: Active customer counts by store or geography; Join customers to payments and rentals for behavior analysis; Customer retention and cohort analyses using create_date

views.name: address_with_geography
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  c.city AS city,
  c.country_id AS country_id,
  ct.country AS country,
  a.postal_code,
  a.phone,
  a.last_update
FROM address a
LEFT JOIN city c ON a.city_id = c.city_id
LEFT JOIN country ct ON c.country_id = ct.country_id
views.description: Addresses enriched with city and country identifiers and names by joining address -> city -> country. One row per address. Useful for geographic analysis and grouping customers/staff/stores by country/city. | Use for: Count customers/staff/stores by country or city; Map revenue or rentals by country or city; Enrich customer records with readable geography for reporting
